items.title: When does carrying the debt cost more than fixing it?
items.description: Models Nadia's actual trade-off from L3: a shortcut's interest cost accumulates every sprint it stays unpaid, while the principal — what it costs to build the proper version — stays roughly fixed regardless of when it's paid down. At the unit's own numbers (principal $9,000, interest $1,200/sprint) the two lines cross around sprint 7.5: past that point, the shortcut has already cost more than it would have to just build it right from the start. Drag sprints elapsed past that break-even point to see cumulative interest overtake the principal, or drag the other two sliders to see how a cheaper/pricier retrofit or a higher/lower per-sprint friction cost shifts where the crossover lands.

params.name: sprintsElapsed
params.label: Sprints the shortcut has stayed unpaid

params.name: interestPerSprint
params.label: Extra friction cost per sprint the shortcut stays

params.name: principalCost
params.label: Cost to build the proper version, whenever it's paid

items.compute: const cumulativeInterest = params.interestPerSprint * params.sprintsElapsed; return { cumulativeInterest, principalCost: params.principalCost };

outputs.label: Cost to fix it properly, right now
